title: stability conservator autoscaler and throughput covenant reporter
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We've seen a recurring class of regressions where short-lived allocation spikes cause the autoscaler to oscillate or prematurely drain dedicated pools, which negatively affects throughput guarantees for tenants. This PR introduces the "stability conservator" autoscaler module and a companion throughput covenant reporter to (1) anchor scaling decisions on a conservative headroom estimate derived from historical occupancy windows, (2) surface signed throughput covenants per-tenant for downstream routing/fallback, and (3) provide high-fidelity utilization decomposition telemetry for postmortem and SLO reporting.

Design highlights: The autoscaler computes a "conservator headroom" using a decayed histogram over the last N minutes of occupancy, combined with an outlier-trimmed peak sketch. Decisions apply a two-stage gating: a quick soft-scale for transient mismatches and a guarded hard-scale requiring confirmation windows. The throughput covenant reporter emits per-tenant percentiles (P50/P95/P99) of served RPS and token throughput mapped to reservation tiers; these are written to telemetry and annotated on the tenant object for routing to prefer lower-latency model variants if guarantees are at risk.

What changed (summary): Added new controller pkg/autoscaler/conservator.go and associated unit tests; introduced telemetry/throughput_covenant.go to compute and emit covenant documents; instrumented pool allocator to read conservator advised headroom; small helm chart changes to expose new flags charts/dedicated/values.yaml; docs/designs/stability-conservator.md detailing the algorithm and rollout notes; e2e/nightly tests exercising burst scenarios and synthetic regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1987) - [x] Unit tests for headroom estimator and gating - [x] Integration tests for allocator fallback behavior - [x] Telemetry backed by histogram + hdr sketch - [x] Canary rollout plan included in docs - [x] Feature flags guarded: autoscaler.enabled, conservator.mode, covenant.reporting=true

Rollout plan: Deploy conservator in passive mode for 48h to stream suggested headroom without influencing scaler; enable active mode in a single pool (canary) for 24h; if SLO regressions observed, rollback via feature flag. The covenant reporter is enabled in read-only reporting initially to allow SRE to tune routing tolerances.

Related: Linear ENG-1987 (design), ENG-2033 (telemetry dashboard), Incident INT-342 (regression that motivated this change).

review_comments: Marco Li: Nice isolation between soft vs hard scale. Please add a short explanation why the decay half-life is set to 4m by default.
Aisha Patel: Reply: Updated conservator.go comments and design doc to justify 4m as tradeoff between responsiveness and smoothing; added unit tests to show sensitivity.
Elena Ortega: Can we ensure these telemetry keys are scrubbed for PII and small tenants don't push cardinality?
Aisha Patel: Reply: covenant reporter buckets by tenant-tier + region (not raw tenant id) in the metrics path; docs updated and scrubber added to hdr_wrapper.go.
Samir Kapoor: observed a flake in e2e where the canary pool scaled down too early; suggested increasing confirmation window to 30s for hard-scale.
Aisha Patel: Reply: Increased confirmation window and added an integration test asserting no hard-scale during synthetic 10s spikes.

release_notes:
Introduces the Stability Conservator autoscaler that computes conservative headroom estimates and a Throughput Covenant reporter that emits per-tenant throughput percentiles. Feature is behind flags and will be canaried. Operators should review docs/designs/stability-conservator.md before enabling.

Impact: Improved autoscaler stability for bursty workloads and richer telemetry for SLA investigations. No breaking changes by default (feature gated).
